new: Copies of stories on the relay: in developer mode (or with &edit), Copy to relay makes an editable copy of a story. Its editor lengthens, shortens or skips chapters, moves when things happen, retimes the narration or takes a new recording, rewrites captions (numbers stay live) and moves sets. The story itself in git never changes.
The studio lists the copies (Copy of ...) and Open plays one. A station in a shared room can run a copy, and a save on one device reaches the others.
Shared rooms: format networks-54. Every device needs this release to join a room.
test: On a laptop with the relay and its password: developer mode, open a story, Copy to relay; stretch a chapter, skip one, rewrite a caption, move a set; Save; reload and check it plays as edited.
In a headset: a story copy opened at a station plays as edited (skipped chapter jumped, captions, the set's place); the story's own still plays as before.
A copy's recording: upload an MP3 in the editor and listen to a stretched chapter (each line starts on its cue, with a pause after it).
untested: Everything in a headset: copies at stations, greyed chapters on the headset's timeline, captions on its panel, moved sets and keep-clear.
How a stretched or shortened chapter's narration sounds (unheard).
A copy's recording on the R2 relay was checked only against the stand-in bucket.
